title: Digital Billboard Pricing - Flexible, Pay-As-You-Go Ads | Blip

facts.fact: Blip pay-as-you-go digital billboard advertising is advertised as starting at $0.01 per display.
Blip digital billboard advertising starts at $0.01 per 8-second play, according to the FAQ.
facts.quote: Blip digital billboard advertising starts at $0.01 per 8-second play.

facts.fact: Blip states it has no monthly minimum and no contract for its digital billboard advertising, and advertisers pay only when the ad displays.
facts.quote: There's no monthly minimum and no contract; you only pay when your ad displays.

facts.fact: Blip states there is no required minimum budget and no contract, and that advertisers can start with just a few dollars per day to test a single market.
facts.quote: You can start with just a few dollars per day to test a single market, then scale based on early performance.

facts.fact: Blip states it does not charge setup fees, platform fees, agency fees, or monthly retainers.
facts.quote: Blip doesn't charge setup fees, platform fees, agency fees, or monthly retainers.

facts.fact: Blip's own page says its platform shows real-time pricing for more than 3,500 digital billboards before a customer commits.
facts.quote: Blip's platform shows real-time pricing for all 3,500+ digital billboards before you commit a dollar.

facts.fact: Blip states that its pricing shows estimated cost per display and traffic data for each location before a campaign launches.
facts.quote: Blip shows pricing for billboard advertising for each location, including estimated cost per display and traffic data.

facts.fact: Blip states that traditional billboard pricing averages $3,953 per month, a figure the page presents without naming a source.
facts.quote: traditional billboard pricing, which averages $3,953 per month and ranges from $250 to $100,000+ depending on market.

facts.fact: Blip states that traditional billboard pricing ranges from $250 to $100,000+ per month depending on market, without naming a source.
facts.quote: ranges from $250 to $100,000+ depending on market.

facts.fact: Blip states that a traditional 4-week digital billboard lease averages $3,953 per month nationally, ranging from $250 in rural markets to $100,000+ in premium urban locations.
facts.quote: A traditional 4-week digital billboard lease averages $3,953 per month nationally and ranges from $250 in rural markets to $100,000+ in premium urban locations.

facts.fact: Blip states that digital billboard pricing is based on 8-second displays, and a 30-second ad is not sold as one block on digital billboards.
facts.quote: A 30-second ad is not sold as one block on digital billboards. Blip uses digital billboard advertising pricing based on 8-second displays.

facts.fact: Blip states that its cost per display varies by location, time of day, and demand.
facts.quote: The cost per display varies based on factors like location, time of day, and demand.

facts.fact: Blip states that high-traffic urban boards carry a higher per-play rate than suburban or rural inventory.
facts.quote: High-traffic urban boards (think downtown Dallas or Atlanta) carry a higher per-play rate than suburban or rural inventory.

facts.fact: Blip states that its marketplace has open ad spots on billboards every day, which it calls blips, and its algorithm uses campaign budgets to bid for them.
facts.quote: Every day, thousands of billboards across the Blip marketplace have open ad spots. We call those spots blips.

facts.fact: Blip reports that customer SafeSiblings.org ran short hourly bursts across 1,000 billboards in hundreds of cities.
facts.quote: By running short, hourly bursts across 1,000 billboards in hundreds of cities
